common_name: Ken Taylor Rosemary (Arching Australian Hedge Rosemary)

planting.note: Set rooted cuttings or container plants in spring or early fall in full sun with sharply drained soil; space generously to allow the arching branches to develop their natural fountain-like form without crowding.

directions: Ken Taylor is an Australian-bred rosemary selection valued for its dense, mounding-to-arching growth habit, intermediate between fully upright culinary types and fully prostrate groundcover forms. Plant in lean, sharply drained soil and avoid overhead irrigation once established, since wet feet in winter are the primary cause of failure in all rosemary types. The long, gracefully arching stems make it a popular choice for informal hedges, low screens, and bank or slope plantings where its spreading mass can be shown off, and it tolerates hard pruning well if a tighter hedge form is wanted. Flowering is prolific and nearly continuous in mild-winter climates, with deep violet-blue flowers that draw bees through the cooler months when few other nectar sources are available. Leaves are fully edible and aromatic, though gardeners seeking the most refined culinary flavor typically still reach for upright cultivars like Tuscan Blue; Ken Taylor shines primarily as a dual-purpose landscape and kitchen plant.
